prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I have not changed my preferred configuration: a single-part B001 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. Round 1 showed six identical configurations, and I again treat that as no argument in itself. What holds up on re-examination is the structure of the claim. Each name maps onto a distinct, identifiable step in the physiology: Holst on the human incretin effect and GLP-1 secretion and action, Mojsov on the identity and synthesis of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, and Drucker on GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology and the translational logic that followed. The mechanism has been confirmed by many independent groups, and large randomised trials show benefit for glycaemia, body weight and cardiovascular and renal endpoints. The discovery is mature, its impact is broad, and the field has clearly changed, which is the standard I would apply to any candidate. The citation should be anchored on physiology and the active peptide, and should name neither a particular drug nor industrial development as the discovery.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point and I have not resolved it. Priority for identifying the active peptide is disputed, and the Habener group is outside the credited names. Knudsen is omitted by the three-person limit, and her analogue chemistry is what made the drugs practical. I would not call that omission free. A citation that rewards the physiology can be read as under-crediting the step that produced the medicines. The chair asks for primary evidence. I have none beyond the shortlist record and my own recollection of the chronology, so I cannot settle the Mojsov and Habener question here. If the committee examined primary papers and found Mojsov's claim materially weaker than I recall, I would reconsider the trio. I would not swap one of the three for Knudsen merely to move toward a drug-development framing, because a swap needs a documented ground for removing a named person.

responses.point: Svenningsson argues that Knudsen's acylation strategy extends a mechanism already established by the others, so she would stay out of the preferred configuration, while recording that this is a judgement and that her case would deserve a hearing under a drug-development framing.
responses.response: I accept the outcome but would argue it differently. The Nobel criterion is a discovery, and the three names carry the physiology and the identity of the peptide. I would be careful with the phrase that she extends an established mechanism, because half-life engineering is what turned a peptide that lasts minutes into a drug. That is a considerable achievement, and it is why I do not call the omission free. I would record it as a judgement made under the three-person limit and made in the citation wording, not as a finding about the relative merit of discovery and development. I also agree with you that a prize with a high public profile must be judged on the science and not on how visible the drugs are.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius says the Mojsov and Habener priority question is the one point that could still change her view of the trio, and asks the committee to examine primary evidence on identification of the active peptide.
responses.response: I agree this is the right test and the evidence behind it should come before any alternative is discussed. What I can add from the supplied record is limited. Mojsov is credited for identifying and synthesising the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) form, and I understand the Habener group's contribution to be the cloning and sequence of the proglucagon gene products. That is a different step, and it is not obviously the same claim. I stress this is my recollection and not a verified finding. If the committee reads the primary papers and concludes the active-form identification was shared closely enough that Mojsov's place cannot be justified, I would want to know which of the three we would replace and on what ground. Until then the claim looks to me distinct enough to hold.

responses.point: Sandberg says the missing Eshhar credit in B045 is a more serious attribution hole than the Mojsov and Habener question, because the omitted person originated the concept.
responses.response: I now agree with this more than I did in round 1, and it affects how I treat B045. I ranked it third in my opening ballot and listed it as the lead alternative, but with the credited trio as supplied I do not see how the committee could defend a CAR-T prize that leaves out the first chimeric receptor work. Narrowing to June and Sadelain does not solve that. The GLP-1 case differs in kind. The disputed question is who identified the active form among groups working on adjacent steps, and the credited names still cover distinct steps of the chain. For CAR-T I would need the Eshhar question settled before I could prefer it, so it remains an alternative and not a second part.

responses.point: Linnarsson placed B004 sixth, saying that the core trio already received Lasker recognition, that the upstream BCR-ABL discoveries lie outside the credited names, and that a prize framed around the drug risks reading as a medicinal-chemistry award.
responses.response: I keep the first of your three objections out of my own reasoning, since a Lasker award is not a Nobel criterion, but I now give more weight to the other two. The upstream chain through Rowley, Witte and Baltimore, and the split between the industrial and academic parts of the compound programme, mean that a Druker, Sawyers and Lydon citation has to be carefully worded around the demonstration that inhibiting the driver kinase treats the disease. That can be done, but your drug-framing concern applies to B004 more than to B001, where the physiological discovery came first. I therefore hold B004 as the second alternative, behind B045 only if the Eshhar question can be settled, and ahead of it if that cannot be settled.

responses.point: El-Manira says that if the committee finds the credit ambiguity among the three too large, he would rather discuss swapping a name than quietly drop the translational half, and that the citation should say explicitly that it is anchored in physiology and peptide identification.
responses.response: I agree with the second half and mostly with the first. The citation should say explicitly that it rests on physiology and on the identity of the active peptide, and the omission of Knudsen should be named as a choice in our deliberation and not hidden by looser wording. On swapping, I would not do it without a specific finding, for example that one of the three did not make the step the citation credits. The evidence the chair asks for could produce such a finding for Mojsov. I do not think it would for Holst, whose human physiology is the secure core, or for Drucker, whose GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology spans the whole field. Absent that, a swap would be a preference about which story the prize should tell, and I do not think we should present it as a scientific conclusion.

uncertainties: Whether primary evidence on identification of the active GLP-1 peptide supports Mojsov's place relative to the Habener group; I rely on recollection and have not verified the chronology.
Whether the committee will accept omitting Knudsen as an explicit judgement under the three-person limit, or will want a documented ground to change the trio.
Whether the Eshhar and Gross omission can be resolved well enough to make B045 a credible fallback if B001 stalls.
Whether the order of my two alternatives, B045 and B004, would change if the committee settled the CAR-T originator question or the upstream BCR-ABL credit.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any credited name on the shortlist is apparent from my profile. My own field is nuclear receptors and midbrain dopamine neurons. My profile records past co-authorship with Svenningsson (about twenty works) and one 2009 paper with El-Manira. I disclose these and do not regard them as conflicts, and neither involves a shortlisted ballot. I do not request recusal. I make no claim of confidential knowledge.
